output.title: When definitions drift, fix one workflow first
output.body:
If your team keeps using the same word three different ways, treat that as a workflow problem before you call it a system problem. The useful question is: which one repeating process shows signs that the same field, label, or category is being interpreted differently each time? That might be invoices, customer records, handoffs, or email triage. Pick one. Do not try to clean up the whole business in one sweep; that is how small problems turn into expensive hobbies.

Then count the drift. For two weeks, track each time someone has to recategorise something, ask for clarification, fix a duplicate record, or rework an approval because the definition was unclear. Count actual instances. Do not guess. Once you can see where the rework sits, you can decide whether the next step is a clearer rule, a better template, or a grounded assistant that checks approved company documents before anything moves forward.

That fit check matters. If the task needs human judgment, policy sign-off, or context outside the written rule, AI is a helper, not a replacement. And for money movement or other high-risk decisions, the owner still approves it. If the workflow and the boundary are both clear, the fix gets a lot less dramatic.
